Hi Sabrina / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and appreciate the clarity on use cases and traffic expectations. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on procurement readiness and commercial path: 

Recap:
- Use case: call summarization + in-app chat for customer support (high throughput daytime).
- Expected ramp: pilot 10k queries/day -> production 100k/day within 3 months.
- Data requirements: customer PII redaction, SOC2 / certs required.

Open questions / asks for procurement path:
1) Billing method: will Acme use PO (net-30) or corporate card?
2) Marketplace: any preference to transact via AWS Marketplace / GCP Marketplace, or direct SOW + PO?
3) Paperwork: who owns SOW/contract redlines? If procurement wants us to draft, I can share a standard SOW + pricing attachment.
4) Timeline: target for signed SOW / PO? You mentioned aiming to close October — is that still accurate?

Next steps from Redwood:
- I’ll attach a sample SOW and an initial quote for the pilot (see attachments).
- If PO required, we can provide an invoice template and send to your AR contact.
- Happy to join a procurement call next week to walk legal/procurement through SOC2 and data controls.

Attachments: redwood-enterprise-pricing.pdf (pricing summary), Acme_Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf (sample SOW)

Would love a short reply with procurement preference (PO vs card), marketplace interest, and who to loop in on the SOW redline.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — great recap. A few quick notes from procurement: 

- Billing: Acme prefers PO (net-30) for any multi-month commitments. We won't be using a corporate card for the pilot/contract.
- Marketplace: we have internal preference to evaluate marketplace options (AWS Marketplace) for ease of procurement, but that requires legal sign-off on the marketplace terms; procurement is open to direct SOW + PO if marketplace timeline is unclear.
- Paperwork: Procurement will take first pass on commercial terms, but Legal may request a few redlines on data residency and liability. If you can provide a draft SOW and a clear list of security artifacts (SOC2, DPA), that would speed review.
- Timeline: Procurement is trying to approve pilot PO within 1-2 weeks, depending on Legal. That's the target — will confirm.

Looping ProcureOps so they have the SOW/quote in their tracker.

Sabrina Liu
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Corp
